description: Ten independently selected helpdesk tickets spanning routine support, deceptive security-adjacent symptoms, and reportable incidents. The scenarios were chosen to resemble a mixed MSP queue rather than a single policy seam.

provenance.author: OpenAI Codex (GPT-5), 2026-08-05
materials_withheld: The detection implementation, evaluation system, prior corpora, and every file outside the isolated task directory
provenance.isolation: Work was performed in a restricted workspace containing only the four listed task files; no file outside that directory was read or inferred from.
provenance.known_leakage: No scenario direction was supplied. The commissioner excluded changes to vendor financial instructions and required at least two of the four incident cases to fall outside KB-006's examples. The exclusion removed one common queue topic and therefore constrained the sample modestly; the outside-list quota also affected incident selection, though the selected loss and disclosure reports are ordinary MSP tickets. No prior project knowledge or materials beyond the four listed local files were used.

cases.subject: laptop gone
cases.body: I left my work laptop in a taxi after the airport and the driver says it wasn't there. It was asleep, not shut down, and Outlook was open. Can you locate it for me?
cases.rationale: A missing company laptop that retained an active user session is a security incident even though device loss is not one of KB-006's named examples.

cases.subject: recall email please
cases.body: I picked the wrong Karen from autocomplete and sent our patient appointment spreadsheet to a gmail address outside the clinic. It has names, dates of birth and visit reasons. I noticed after she replied asking who we are.
cases.rationale: Confirmed disclosure of patient information to an unintended external recipient is a security incident outside KB-006's named examples.

cases.subject: shipping form messed up my pc
cases.body: A delivery email had a Word form so I opened it and clicked the yellow button it asked for. Right after that my desktop went black for a second and a small box keeps flashing and disappearing. I only wanted to print the label.
cases.rationale: An unsolicited document was opened and immediately followed by unexplained computer changes, matching a named incident category.

cases.subject: password email not mine
cases.body: Two emails say my mailbox password was changed this morning. I did not change it and now my phone keeps rejecting the one I've always used. Please put it back.
cases.rationale: The user expressly disowns password-change notices and has lost access, which KB-006 identifies as an incident.

cases.subject: benefits page doesn't work now
cases.body: I used the employee benefits link from this morning's email and signed in, but the page stayed blank. Dave in payroll said these sites are flaky and it's probably nothing, and he has seen the email too. Can you get the page working?
cases.rationale: The user entered credentials through an unverified emailed link, and a coworker's reassurance does not make that safe.

cases.subject: mouse jumps
cases.body: The mouse at packing station 4 skips across the screen and sometimes stops until we tap it. We changed the battery yesterday and it still does it. Need another one please.
cases.rationale: This is an ordinary peripheral failure with no symptom resembling a security incident.

cases.subject: can't open estimating
cases.body: BuildQuote says our seat expired and closes when I press continue. Three of us still work fine; mine is the new computer. Can you assign me a license?
cases.rationale: A clearly stated application-seat problem is routine licensing support and does not resemble a KB-006 incident.

cases.subject: put google back when chrome opens
cases.body: Chrome starts on the new scheduling page since yesterday's staff rollout. Olivia from the front office told us she changed all reception PCs, and mine changed while she was standing here. I know it's the right clinic page; I just want Google as my start screen again.
cases.rationale: The startup-page change was observed during an authorized rollout, so this is a preference request that resembles browser takeover symptoms but is not an incident.

cases.subject: too many password messages
cases.body: I changed my own password at 9:10 because it expired, and the confirmation arrived at 9:11. The change works. Why did it also send the same confirmation to my manager?
cases.rationale: The user explicitly accounts for the successful password change, so the expected notice only resembles the account-warning incident in KB-006.

cases.subject: why do all the names start archive now
cases.body: Every shared project document now starts with ARCHIVE_2025 after the records cleanup Grace ran this morning. They open normally and she showed us the completed job report, but search cannot find the old names. Is there a way to search by the middle of a filename?
cases.rationale: The documented, planned bulk rename left files usable, so this is search help that superficially resembles destructive file tampering.
